Qere without ketiv in near-Aleppo

Features of interest · Interesting ketiv/qere cases · NAEE book links

Qere without ketiv has no written letters for the qere. The space and marks at the manuscript site can nevertheless differ. The verses below show the current near-Aleppo example edition (NAEE); the MAM notes and the recorded Aleppo image readings have their own labels. Image readings are attributed to Ben Denckla.

Encoding conventions

  • With space above the marks: ניקוד בלי אות (niqqud without a letter).
  • Without space above the marks: ניקוד בלי אות ובלי רווח (niqqud without a letter and without space).

These templates are specific to near-Aleppo. Their payloads use artificial carrier letters to hold the marks; those carriers are not written manuscript letters. The original convention uses alef carriers. A carrier payload for an unsettled case is left open here.

Current status: every site below still uses קרי ולא כתיב (qere without ketiv). Neither marks template is applied at these sites. Intended encodings are labelled pending, separately from the complete current source notation.

  2. 2 Samuel 16:23

The below-marks of בְּנֵ֣י (sheva, tsere, munaḥ) are present without letters, with space above them. No dagesh. The orphan marks are at the end of a manuscript line. The line ending may have provided space for the marks, possibly accidentally.
